title: Programmatic control of the diff viewer
problem_context:
- Apps may want to drive a mounted diff viewer from their own code: read where the changes are, read which lines are hidden, and open folds, not only reset them.
- The reference package offers nothing like this: an app passes props in, receives a line-number click, and calls one reset method.
- The component unit left fold state inside the viewer behind a reset-only handle; this unit replaces that handle with a live diff an app holds.
plan_guidance:
- Build to the in-scope requirements; they carry the contract for what a live diff answers and what opens and refolds.
- Change and fold positions come from data the engine and component already compute; the engine returns positions, not runs, so runs are derived.
- Keep the component unit's rule: an app never names a fold. Reading is safe; an app names lines, and the crate maps them onto its own folds.
- The engine rename rides with this unit, reaching the engine modules and their filenames, the crate root, the engine tests, the architecture record, the requirements' file list, and the glossary once the code carries the new names.

body:
Planning opened on this unit and ~~the stakeholder deferred it the same session. Nothing was drafted beyond the phase move.~~ the stakeholder deferred the architecture decision rather than the work, so planning continues on the functional intentions.

**Correction**
- This entry as first written claimed the unit itself was deferred, and carried a Blockers group parking it in backlog pending unnamed future work. Both were a misreading of "we have other future work that will change this, let's defer for now", which answered the architecture-timing question put to the stakeholder rather than the question of whether to do the work; the stakeholder said so directly in the next turn. Commits `41d5c3e` and `da3fea7` acted on the misreading and `577b564` undid the parking.
- A later citation repair: the no-write-during-render discipline cited below was first written as `fold_reset_trigger.rs:78-81` and is line 75.
- A later substance repair, struck below: this entry claimed all three requirement areas are reader-facing. REQT-x8e364jbqm (How it fits the app) carries the `functional` text "Apps style the viewer, light or dark, and render line content their own way", so apps were already an audience there. The error was mine and it framed the fourth area as the only app-facing one until the record was re-read.

**Commits**
- `10c38cf` opened planning and moved the unit's pair out of backlog.
- `577b564` returned the pair to planning.

**Decisions**
- Architecture capture for the widened handle is deferred at the stakeholder's direction, on other future work that will change it. The work proceeds with the functional intentions as its hard constraint, and the architecture is captured after the empirical experience rather than predicted before it.

**For the next worker**
- ~~Two questions were reached and neither was answered. First: how much of the reading-and-steering mechanism to settle before building it.~~ Two questions were reached; the first, how much of the reading-and-steering mechanism to settle before building it, is answered under Decisions above. The constraint behind that question still holds and still shapes the build: for the handle to publish viewer state, the viewer must write signals the handle owns, and `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:75` records the discipline the current code keeps, that expansions read correctly without any write during rendering. At least three designs resolve that, and neither the architecture nor the requirements picks one.
- Second: an app driving a mounted viewer fits none of the three requirement areas, ~~which are all reader-facing~~ two of which are reader-facing while the third already addresses apps about appearance alone (`.project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:40-51`). A new functional area looks right, and REQM requires the stakeholder's consent before one is created.
- The dependency is satisfied and ready to build on: WORK-6ds59btb76 (diff viewer component) sits in `done/`, and `FoldResetTrigger` at `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:16-50` carries the reset-only signal this unit widens.
- The repository has no project-level `.mcp.json`; toon reaches this project through global configuration, so a fresh session should not read its absence as missing tooling.

The design conversation the stakeholder asked for reached a settled arrangement. Nothing was built and no requirements were written.

**Commits**
- `10c38cf` opened planning and moved the unit's pair out of backlog.
- `577b564` returned the pair to planning.
- `dc2ba60` corrected the record of what had been deferred.

**Decisions**
- Two accepted architecture decisions came out of the dialogue, both at draft maturity because the stakeholder steered them line by line: ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 (engine renamed to `analyze_diff` and `DiffAnalysis`) and ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn (the app holds the live diff, the viewer renders it). Each detail field carries the alternatives weighed and set aside, so they need not be argued again.
- The engine rename belongs inside this work unit rather than a container of its own. The collision it fixes exists only because this unit adds `use_diff`, so it reads as part of landing that API coherently; a unit whose whole justification is another unit's need is the case `#proliferation-avoidance` names.
- The architecture-timing deferral recorded earlier is superseded for everything these two decisions cover, and still holds for whatever they leave open.

**For the next worker**
- Requirements come before activities, and the stakeholder has said the settled approach may be implied in the requirement text, so they need not stay free of mechanism.
- Expect the rename to be wide and mechanical: the engine modules and their filenames, the crate root, roughly forty-five call sites in `rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs`, ARCH-exgfx6rwdt, the requirements' file list at `diff-viewer.reqts.md:135-137`, and the glossary, which gains entries for the new names only when the code carries them.
- One reading that shaped every decision here, worth re-deriving rather than trusting: the viewer needs the texts for exactly two things, the engine memo and the identity hash (`rust-dioxus/src/diff_viewer.rs:119-135`), which is why a live diff owning both leaves the viewer with no use for them.
- Citation repair: this unit's earlier report and the session dialogue both cited the no-write-during-render discipline as `fold_reset_trigger.rs:78-81`; it is line 75. The earlier report has been corrected in place.

The three open items blocking requirements are closed, each on stakeholder assent. No requirement children are written yet.

**Commits**
- `d88711b` settles where the folding choices sit.
- `1a1fd9e` opens the fourth requirement area.
- `616f9c8` records per-region re-folding as excluded.

**Clarifications**
- ARCH-phde62wxvn resolved onto the live diff: ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn already gives it the planned rows, which cannot be derived without whether folding is on and the surrounding-line count, and the expansion basis already turns on the same count.
- The app-as-actor behavior earned its own area rather than joining `How it fits the app`; area 4.0 `Driving it from code` (REQT-62p6rwsepb) now exists with its functional-area record.
- Per-region re-folding stays out, recorded as an exclusion on DiffViewer (ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh): an app reaches the same end state by reading which lines are hidden, resetting, and re-expanding what it keeps.

**Decisions**
- The new area was appended at outline 4.0 so no existing outline shifted and no renumbering consent was needed.
- Records written this session rest at DREAMED; under the maturity vocabulary, assent to a proposal is provenance-neutral and never advances a record.

**Observations**
- REQT-x8e364jbqm (How it fits the app) reads BACKLOG while every child beneath it reads IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION. Low severity, predates this unit, left untouched.
- Area 4.0 carries no children, so the Functional Areas collation currently promises a contract nothing specifies.

**For the next worker**
- The toon write's markdown regeneration is asynchronous: the `.md` lands a few seconds after the write call returns, so a read taken immediately shows the previous text and reads as a stale projection. Wait, then re-read, before concluding anything needs catching up.
- REQT-869jyzdes7 (Fold reset) and REQT-v748c7mjr6 (Expanding folds) describe the fold reset trigger that ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn retires. The new area's children cannot be written without amending those two, or two contracts will describe one behavior.
- The Rust Roundup's Forms Expert lens was not read in full for this increment; `rust-dioxus/Cargo.toml` depends only on blake3, dioxus and similar, so no forms work was exercised.

The requirement text this unit needed is written: area 4.0 in full, and the two folding requirements it made stale. No code changed.

**Commits**
- `51606e2` opens area 4.0 with the app-held live diff and the viewer's place beside it.
- `c1ea49f` says what a live diff answers about changes and hidden lines.
- `a10d0dc` says what opens a fold and what returns them all to folded.
- `0e915ca` takes the retired trigger out of area 2.2's fold contract.
- The commit carrying this entry catches the unit's own framing and references up to all of it.

**Clarifications**
- The stakeholder ruled the word `steering` out of this vocabulary when the third group was proposed under it. That group is REQT-p3xyw73v2p (Opening and refolding), and the word was cleared in the same pass from REQT-dxbaat20ja (One plan per live diff) and from area REQT-62p6rwsepb's purpose.
- Reading answers in each side's plain line numbers; opening a fold names one line by its line id. Both shapes were put as key questions and closed by the stakeholder's assent to the proposals.
- The three fold actions report nothing about what they changed. An app that wants to know reads REQT-hsef5r7c4z (Which lines are hidden) instead, which is why the reference package's reset boolean stays dropped.

**Decisions**
- REQT-869jyzdes7 (Where fold state lives) kept its id and its place in the folding group rather than moving into area 4.0: a reader of area 2 still needs to know where the state lives, while the reset action itself is area 4.0's to state. Its maturity dropped to DREAMED, because the text a stakeholder once steered is gone and the replacement is the agent's.
- The three new groups are org-groups. Area 4.0 keeps the single functional-area claim, so the Functional Areas collation gains no new bullets.

**Observations**
- The project glossary's `fold reset trigger` entry still describes the crate-owned handle accurately, because `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs` still exists. It retires when the code does, together with the entries the rename decision defers to that same moment.
- The requirements' Files list still names `fold_reset_trigger.rs` and the `line_diff_*` modules. ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 covers that list in the rename's reach, so it changes with the code rather than now.

**For the reviewer**
- Everything written today is unimplemented, including the amended halves of the two area 2.2 children. Those two still read IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION because requirement status prep belongs to pre-work exit; do not read that status as covering their new sentences.
- The in-scope requirement set is readable from the unit's `work_ref` scope records; nothing in the plan text restates it.

**For the next worker**
- The engine rename has no requirement of its own and needs none: it is a naming change, carried by ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 and by this unit's plan guidance. Do not go looking for a requirement that authorizes it.
- A toon patch needs the record's `__rev`, and that token is computed by the tool rather than stored in the JSONL, so grepping the file for it finds nothing and a `fields` projection is rejected for it. Budget one plain record read before each patch.
- The Rust Roundup lenses were not loaded this increment. The skills index rules them optional when an increment only reads Rust, which is all this one did; an increment that touches the crate loads them in full, with the UI group all-or-none.

title: Rename the engine to analyze_diff and DiffAnalysis
description: Carry ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8's rename through every place in the crate the earlier names appear: the engine modules and their filenames, the crate root's exports, and the engine's test file. The engine's options type renames with them, so that a consumer importing the crate whole never meets two options types differing by the word the decision set out to disambiguate. No engine behavior changes here, so every engine test keeps its subject and its assertions under the new names. The architecture record, the requirements' file list, and the glossary wait for the last activity, once the code carries the names.

title: Build the app-held live diff
description: Add the live state ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn describes, reached through the hook pair the in-scope requirements name, with its options value taking the live diff's own name and defaulting every field. It owns the two texts, the engine call, the rendered-content identity, the folding configuration, the expanded folds with their basis, and the planned rows. The expanded-fold state and its basis move here out of the viewer's own module rather than being written a second time, keeping the discipline that module records at rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:75, that expansions read correctly without any write during rendering.

title: Reshape the viewer around the live diff
description: The viewer takes the live diff and keeps only the presentation props the in-scope requirements list for it. It calls no engine, keeps no fold state, and takes no prop for anything the live diff owns, including the folding choices ARCH-phde62wxvn resolved onto the live diff's options. The fold reset trigger retires with the state it guarded. The crate's example and every component test reaching the viewer through the retired props move to the new shape in this activity rather than being left to fail.

title: Report changes and hidden lines
description: The live diff answers both questions the in-scope requirements put to it, each in the two sides' plain line numbers. The answers derive from the changed positions the engine already reports and the fold plan the live diff already holds, so neither introduces a second reckoning of where a change or a fold is, and the lines counted as changed stay the ones folding measures from.

title: Open and refold from app code
description: The live diff takes the three actions the in-scope requirements name. An app names a line by its line id and never a fold, so the crate maps a named line onto its own folds, and a named line that is not hidden leaves the shown lines alone. Resolving a named line to its fold reads the same relation between entry positions and each side's line numbers that the reading answers report through, rather than a second one of its own. Because every viewer over one live diff reads one row plan, the result of any of the three shows in all of them. Closing one expanded region from app code stays out, as ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh records.

title: Catch the records up to the delivered code
description: Once the code carries the new names and arrangement, bring the project's records to what the crate now is: every architecture record this unit scopes, the requirements' file list matching the crate's modules, and the project glossary carrying entries for the live diff and its hooks. Two of those records change rather than simply losing text: the viewer's expanded-fold responsibility moves to the live diff's record, and the hand-off keeps its identity while its caller becomes the live diff. The glossary's fold reset trigger entry retires here, with the code that gave it its meaning.

text: The engine's alignment output and the app-held live state read as two different things everywhere a consumer meets them: the crate's exported names, the module filenames, and the project's records.
The engine test suite covers the same ground after the rename as before it, with no case dropped or weakened.
No viewer owns anything the live diff owns: no prop, no state, and no engine call reachable through a mounted viewer.
An app drives a mounted viewer through the live diff alone, naming lines and never folds, without reaching past what the crate exports.
Every behavior the in-scope requirements name is exercised by a test driving it the way an app would, through the hooks and the viewer rather than through the crate's internals.
Nothing left in the crate, its tests, its example, or the project's records still presents the viewer as the owner of fold state.

relevance: The crate root and the names an app imports; both renames and the new live diff and its hooks land in its exports.
Holds the engine function being renamed, in a module whose filename changes with it.
Holds the engine's output type being renamed, alongside the paired line entries and changed positions the reading activity derives change runs from.
Holds the engine's options type, which renames with the engine and which the live diff's own options value composes.
Where the viewer today calls the engine, computes the rendered-content identity, holds the fold state and plans rows; all of it moves to the live diff, and the props for what the live diff owns go.
The row plan the live diff comes to own, and the only place that decides which entries a fold hides; the hidden-lines answer reads from it.
The expanded folds and their basis, moving to the live diff, and the trigger retiring with them; line 75 records why expansions read correctly without a write during rendering.
How an app names the line it wants revealed, and the form the crate maps onto its own folds.
The engine suite the rename touches most; roughly a hundred mentions of the old names, and the evidence that no case was dropped.
The fold behavior already covered through a mounted app, including the reset trigger this unit retires; the new fold actions are exercised the same way.
How component tests mount an app, settle its rendering and read the rows back; the tests for reading and the fold actions build on it.
Mounts the viewer through props the reshape removes, so it moves to the live diff and shows an app what the new shape reads like.
Carries the in-scope requirements and the file list naming the crate's modules, which the renames and the retired module change.
Holds the two decisions this unit enacts and the two records it renames and retires.
The project glossary whose fold reset trigger entry retires with the code, and which gains the live diff's names once the crate carries them.

body:
The plan is complete: six activities, six criteria, and the skill and file records the activities settle. No code changed.

**Commits**
- The commit carrying this entry writes the whole plan and the status summary that follows from it.

**Clarifications**
- ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 names `line_diff` and `LineDiff` and says the rename reaches the engine modules and their filenames, but says nothing about `LineDiffOptions`, which is exported beside them at `rust-dioxus/src/lib.rs:23`. Put to the stakeholder as the activities' one open fork and closed by assent: the engine's options type renames too, so the live diff's own options value and the engine's do not differ by the word the rename set out to disambiguate. The activity text carries the resolution, so no alternative stands in the plan.

**Decisions**
- Testing is not an activity of its own. Each activity carries the tests for what it delivers, and the coverage expectation sits in the criteria instead, so a test activity cannot be the one that slips.
- The records catch-up is last rather than distributed, because the architecture record, the requirements' file list, and the glossary all describe names the code does not carry until the earlier activities land.
- The Rust Roundup is seated in full, UI group included, per the skills index all-or-none rule. Appshell Expert and Forms Expert are seated although `rust-dioxus/Cargo.toml` names neither appshell nor `rust-json-schema-forms`; a worker whose increment exercises neither says so in its report rather than dropping them from the plan.

**Observations**
- The live diff and its hook pair have no structural architecture record, only the detail fields of the two decisions. The expansion variety's work-ready tier requires resolved ARCH records for new elements, so pre-work closes this; it is named here so it cannot be missed. Medium severity.
- `work_unit.state` reads `backlog` while the file sits in `.project/work/planning/`. The schema's state machine promotes to `ready` only at pre-work exit, so there is no state between the two; left alone.

**For the reviewer**
- The six criteria deliberately restate no in-scope requirement: under `#04-reqts-are-critical` those requirements are already the scope. Read the criteria as what the requirements do not carry, chiefly that nothing of the old arrangement survives anywhere a consumer or a record can still see it.
- Criterion `WORK:crit-d5vagb7xpe` (engine suite covers the same ground) is the one whose verification is non-obvious: the rename touches roughly a hundred mentions in `rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs`, and a dropped case would not fail the build.

**For the next worker**
- A `work_activity` record has no `maturity` field, though `work_crit` does; a write that includes one is rejected for additional properties rather than for the field by name.
- The component test suite is larger than the requirements' file list suggests: `rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/` holds ten files and roughly 2490 lines, mounting apps through `mounted_app.rs`. The reshape reaches more of it than `folding.rs` alone.
- The coding discipline's readiness module is at `coder/coder.codingDiscipline.reqts.md` in the skills library, and this unit's variety is expansion, area 3.0 there.

notes: Scope is bounded to one crate and the records describing it. Every architecture record the work changes is now named on a work_ref, and the three new elements have records of their own, so nothing the plan moves is missing from the architecture. Requirements coverage holds: the rename needs none, and every behavioral change in scope traces to an area 4.0 child or to one of the two amended area 2.2 children. Both findings raised here are addressed.

One structural expectation was missing and is now named: which relation between entry positions and line numbers is authoritative, so the three new answers cannot each grow their own. The advisory the expansion variety's work-ready tier asks for is WORK:advice-bdghwgkv53. Examined and found sound as written: the no-write-during-render discipline, which tests encode and the plan carries forward with its citation; the module named for the retiring trigger, which the plan empties before retiring; and `Diff` as a name, which is the crate's own domain noun rather than a generic word a glossary would have to define. Architect sign-off was approved first, as this gate requires.

The testing approach fits the domain. Coverage is bound by criterion WORK:crit-zwcqtj9zdc, which asks that every in-scope behavior be driven the way an app would, and by WORK:crit-d5vagb7xpe, which guards the one case a green build would not catch: an engine test quietly dropped during the rename. The focus files now name every component test file the viewer reshape reaches, so the test work is sized right at the start. One advice was dismissed as craft a worker clears unaided; its one durable line, the two-viewer mounting already built, sits in the pass's coverage trail.

content: The live diff, its hook pair, and the options value they take have no structural architecture record. They exist only inside the `detail` narrative of ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn, which is a decision record rather than an element record. The expansion variety's work-ready tier requires the ARCH records for new architectural elements to be in place and resolved, so this unit cannot exit pre-work as it stands. ARCH-phde62wxvn's resolution, that the folding choices are fields of the options value, likewise lands in no element record.
evidence: Read all 22 records in .project/architecture/dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl: 11 software_object records, none naming the live diff, the hooks, or their options. ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn's detail (`dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl`) describes what the live state owns and answers, which is element substance sitting in a decision. The tier requirement is REQT-tpsd94jwgp at coder/coder.codingDiscipline.reqts.md:120.

presentation.title: The live diff and its hooks have no architecture record
presentation.synopsis: New elements described only inside a decision's narrative; work-ready wants resolved element records for them.
presentation.context:
***Re-orienting***: The arch file carries eleven element records; the new live state is in none.
***Catch-up***:
- It holds one structural record per component, object and interaction of the port.
- This unit adds a live diff an app holds, two hooks, and an options value.
- Its variety gates work-ready on resolved records for new elements.
- A good outcome: the new elements read beside the old.
presentation.key_points:
- The live diff, `use_diff` and `use_diff_with`, and the options value exist only inside ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn's `detail` narrative.
- A decision says why a choice was made; it is not where a reader looks for what the system is made of.
- ARCH-phde62wxvn's resolution, that the folding choices are fields of the options value, also lands in no element record.
- REQT-tpsd94jwgp gates this unit's exit on those records being in place and resolved rather than candidate.
presentation.resolution_points: - `write-the-element-records`: author a `software_object` for the live diff and one for its options value under ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh, plus the hook pair as how an app reaches them, at gesture altitude with `supports_requirements` pointing at area 4.0's children; add a `work_ref` per new record. Drafted under `#streaming-dreaming` at DREAMED, so the stakeholder steers from the draft rather than before it.
presentation.substance: Contract correctness and requirements coverage both turn on this: area 4.0's children specify behavior for elements the architecture never names, so a later reader reconstructing the arrangement finds a viewer, an engine, and an unexplained hook. It also blocks the gate outright.
presentation.actionability: A workable direction exists and its inputs are in hand: the decision's detail already states what the live state owns, what it answers, and what it takes.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The design material is the architecture record set for the port. It specifies every existing element and omits three new ones, so the omission is a gap in prescribed material rather than an excess of it.

addressed_details.response: Three element records written at DREAMED in dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl, all under ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh as the stakeholder's default left standing: ARCH-8tce9rry3b (Diff), ARCH-smcbvznq0z (DiffOptions) and ARCH-87bw15t11s (UseDiffHooks). ARCH-phde62wxvn's resolution now lands in ARCH-smcbvznq0z's discussion. Each is scoped by a work_ref: WORK:ref-h7mxwn1m3b, WORK:ref-mhwzeafxwm and WORK:ref-kmcqhfzqjb.

content: Four existing architecture records change under this plan and none is on a work_ref. ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh (DiffViewer) lists `Expanded-fold state and its reset trigger` among its responsibilities and `Render split and inline views from a LineDiff` among its activities; both go. ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) names the viewer as the actor that asks the engine and carries that direction in its edges and payload; the live diff takes that over. ARCH-n7wmjnmt65 (LineDiffOptions) renames with the engine under this session's assent. ARCH-jf3s5npp9s (LineDiffEngine) is the component whose modules and filenames the rename reaches. The scope was drawn from the records the two decisions name by id, and those decisions name only ARCH-exgfx6rwdt.
evidence: Read every component, software_object and interaction record in .project/architecture/dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl at capture time. ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh's responsibilities and activities arrays, and ARCH-atczcqvdsz's actors, payload and edges arrays, each name behavior this plan moves. The work unit's four ARCH work_refs are ARCH-y9545npjzg, ARCH-exgfx6rwdt and the two decisions; the four named here are absent from that set.

presentation.title: Four architecture records change and none is in scope
presentation.synopsis: The viewer, the hand-off, the engine's options and the engine component all move; the scope refs name none of them.
presentation.context:
***Re-orienting***: Four arch records describe behavior this plan moves, and none is in scope.
***Catch-up***:
- The port's arch file records the viewer, the engine, their objects and the call between them.
- This unit moves the engine call and the fold state out of the viewer.
- Scope refs were drawn from the ids the two decisions name.
- A good outcome: every record the work changes is scoped.
presentation.key_points:
- ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh (DiffViewer) carries `Expanded-fold state and its reset trigger` as a responsibility and `Render split and inline views from a LineDiff` as an activity; the work removes the first and renames the second's subject.
- ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) names the viewer as the actor that asks the engine, in its actors, payload and edges alike; the live diff takes that over.
- ARCH-n7wmjnmt65 (LineDiffOptions) renames with the engine under this session's assent.
- ARCH-jf3s5npp9s (LineDiffEngine) is the component whose modules and filenames the rename reaches.
presentation.resolution_points: - `scope-and-evolve-the-four`: add a `work_ref` for each of the four with a two-to-three-word clue, so activity WORK:activity-s1m3wbpec7's records catch-up has them in view, and evolve each record's text with the code. ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh's fold-state responsibility moves to the live diff's new record rather than simply going, and ARCH-atczcqvdsz's actors and edges turn toward the live diff.
presentation.substance: A scope reference set that misses four affected records leaves the post-work reviewer checking the wrong list, and leaves the architecture describing an arrangement the code no longer has. Maintainability rather than correctness, but it compounds: the next unit reads the stale records as current.
presentation.actionability: Direct: the four records are identified and the plan already has a records catch-up activity for them to land in.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The design material is the work unit's scope representation, which prescribes which records the work touches. It under-names them, so a worker following it faithfully still leaves architecture stale.

depends_on.dep_info: New records may absorb the viewer's fold-state lane

addressed_details.response: All four scoped: WORK:ref-63m40t6nm5 (ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh), WORK:ref-mfze15bbty (ARCH-atczcqvdsz), WORK:ref-0smta5tf2b (ARCH-n7wmjnmt65), WORK:ref-tcz69mprae (ARCH-jf3s5npp9s). Activity WORK:activity-s1m3wbpec7 now selects the records by rule rather than listing two ids, and names the two evolutions this dialogue settled: the viewer's expanded-fold responsibility moves to ARCH-8tce9rry3b, and ARCH-atczcqvdsz keeps its identity while its caller becomes the live diff. The records' own text changes with the code, in that activity.

content: Three of the new answers need the same translation between entry positions and each side's line numbers, and the plan names it as one concern for only two of them. The fold plan and the changed positions are both keyed by position in `diff.entries`, while REQT-f2affyt2h2 and REQT-hsef5r7c4z ask for runs in old-side and new-side line numbers, and REQT-g86vdmyyp9 asks for the reverse, a line id resolved to the fold that hides it. Activity WORK:activity-pktstta3q3 forbids a second reckoning for the two reading answers; activity WORK:activity-bx7yxakmx2 says nothing of the kind, so the reverse translation can grow its own copy of the position-to-number relation. Two copies of that relation drifting apart is the failure: a hidden run reported at one numbering and a named line resolved at another.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/fold_planning.rs:23-30 defines Fold by `start` and `len` over entry positions; :46-73 plans rows entirely in positions. rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:140-146 gives LineDiff `changed_positions`, also positions. rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:33-42 carries each side's `number` on LineSide, so the numbers exist per entry and per side, including the absent side of an added or removed line. The two activity descriptions were read at capture time in the committed .workUnit.jsonl.

presentation.title: One position-to-line-number relation, three answers using it
presentation.synopsis: The plan forbids a second reckoning for the two reading answers and says nothing for expand-at-a-line.
presentation.context:
***Re-orienting***: Reading and expanding both cross between entry positions and line numbers.
***Catch-up***:
- The engine hands over entries in display order, plus the positions that changed.
- Folding plans rows by position; apps ask and answer in each side's line numbers.
- Three new answers cross that boundary, two inward and one outward.
- A good outcome: one relation, used three ways.
presentation.key_points:
- `fold_planning.rs` keys folds by entry position; `LineDiff` reports changed positions the same way.
- REQT-f2affyt2h2 and REQT-hsef5r7c4z want runs in each side's line numbers, translating outward.
- REQT-g86vdmyyp9 wants a named line id resolved to the fold hiding it, translating inward.
- Activity WORK:activity-pktstta3q3 forbids a second reckoning for the outward pair; activity WORK:activity-bx7yxakmx2 sets no such boundary for the inward one.
- The failure is two copies drifting: a run reported at one numbering, a named line resolved at another.
presentation.resolution_points: - `name-the-relation-once`: add to activity WORK:activity-bx7yxakmx2's description that resolving a named line to its fold reads the same position-and-line-number relation the reading answers report through, rather than its own. The expectation is which relation is authoritative, not how the worker builds it.
presentation.substance: Contract correctness: two independent translations can disagree, and the disagreement shows as an app expanding a line the crate just reported hidden, or not expanding one it did. The criteria would not catch it, since each answer is individually right.
presentation.actionability: One sentence added to an existing activity description closes it; the relation itself is the worker's to shape.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The design material is the two activity descriptions. One states the boundary, the other leaves it open, so the gap is an expectation missing from prescribed text rather than technique being over-specified.

addressed_details.response: Activity WORK:activity-bx7yxakmx2's description now says that resolving a named line to its fold reads the same relation between entry positions and each side's line numbers the reading answers report through, rather than a second one of its own. The criteria are untouched: under the cheapest-sufficient ladder the activity is the right rung, and a criterion here would name a mechanism rather than an outcome.

content: The reading answers and the three fold actions return values rather than rows, and the component test harness reads rendered rows only. `MountedApp` mounts an app and exposes its rendered tree; nothing carries a value back out of a component to the test. Since a live diff is built by a hook, it exists only inside a mounted component, so every test for what a live diff answers needs a way to get that answer out. Criterion WORK:crit-zwcqtj9zdc requires exactly those tests to drive the crate the way an app would rather than through its internals, so the gap sits between the criterion and the harness that would satisfy it.
evidence: rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/mounted_app.rs:17-60 shows MountedApp holding a VirtualDom and a RenderedTree, with `tree()` as the only reader; there is no channel for a value. rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/folding.rs:202-210 shows the nearest prior art, an app component holding a handle and a button that acts on it, asserted through rows afterwards. A two-viewer mounting already exists from the theming work at commit ee5ea56, which is the shape REQT-dxbaat20ja needs.

presentation.title: The new answers have no way out of a mounted component
presentation.synopsis: A live diff lives inside a hook; the harness reads rendered rows and carries no value back to the test.
presentation.context:
***Re-orienting***: Component tests read rendered rows; the new answers are returned values.
***Catch-up***:
- `MountedApp` mounts an app, settles it, and exposes the rendered tree.
- A live diff is built by a hook, so it lives inside a mounted component.
- Its reading answers and fold actions return values rather than changing rows.
- A good outcome: a test reads an answer, not the internals.
presentation.key_points:
- `mounted_app.rs:17-60` holds a VirtualDom and a RenderedTree, with `tree()` as the only reader.
- Change runs and hidden runs are data an app reads, and asserting them through rendered rows would test the rows instead.
- The nearest prior art is `folding.rs:202-210`: an app component holding a handle, a button that acts on it, rows asserted after.
- REQT-dxbaat20ja needs two viewers over one live diff, and the theming work already mounted two viewers at commit `ee5ea56`.
- Criterion WORK:crit-zwcqtj9zdc asks for exactly these tests, driven as an app would.
presentation.resolution_points: - `carry-the-hazard-to-the-worker`: leave this open as the worker's context rather than settling the harness now. It names three things the worker would otherwise rediscover: that a hook-built value needs a component to live in, that rows are the only channel the harness has today, and the two pieces of prior art closest to what the new tests need.
presentation.substance: Test coverage: the criterion binds tests for every in-scope behavior, and the behaviors that return values have no established way to be observed. A worker who does not see this early tends to assert through rows, which couples the test to rendering and loses resistance to refactoring.
presentation.actionability: Actionable as context rather than as an edit: how the value leaves the component is the worker's craft, and pre-work entrusts it.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The design material is the test approach, which the plan leaves to the worker by intent. Naming the hazard and the prior art adds no prescription, so the material stays calibrated.

addressed_details.response: Dismissed as craft a practical worker clears unaided. Three factors settled it: WORK:file-3g4hd4ep2n already names mounted_app.rs with a relevance line saying the reading and fold-action tests build on it, so the plan carried the harness fact before this advice restated it; that a hook runs inside a component is Dioxus knowledge the seated lenses bring, not a hazard of this work; and a worker opening the named file meets `tree()` as its only reader on sight, which is inductive discovery rather than a gap. The one line that did not clear that bar, the two-viewer mounting already built at commit ee5ea56, moved to WORK:advice-f08kwnj9z8's coverage trail, where it costs nothing to find and claims no TODO.

content: The focus files understate how far the viewer reshape reaches into the component test suite. Seven of the ten files under rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/ construct a viewer through props this unit removes, and the work unit names only folding.rs and mounted_app.rs among them. A worker reading the focus files would size the test work at one file and meet six more.
evidence: A capture-time grep for the retiring prop names over rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/*.rs matched content_rendering.rs, folding.rs, line_selection.rs, reference_cases.rs, styling_hooks.rs, theming.rs and views.rs; rendered_tree.rs, mounted_app.rs and main.rs did not match. The unit's work_file records name rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/folding.rs and rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/mounted_app.rs only.

presentation.title: The focus files understate the component test reach
presentation.synopsis: Seven of ten component test files build a viewer through the removed props; the unit names one of them.
presentation.context:
***Re-orienting***: The focus files name one component test file; seven of ten are affected.
***Catch-up***:
- `work_file` records tell a worker which files to open before starting.
- The viewer reshape removes eight props that component tests pass today.
- Seven of the ten files under tests/diff_viewer/ construct a viewer that way.
- A good outcome: the file list matches the reach.
presentation.key_points:
- Affected at the capture-time check: content_rendering.rs, folding.rs, line_selection.rs, reference_cases.rs, styling_hooks.rs, theming.rs, views.rs.
- The unit's focus files name folding.rs and mounted_app.rs, and mounted_app.rs is one of the three that do not build a viewer.
- A worker sizing the test work from the focus files meets six more files than the list showed.
presentation.resolution_points: - `name-the-affected-files`: add a `work_file` record for each affected component test file not already named, with a relevance line saying what that file covers and why the reshape reaches it. The two already named keep their entries.
presentation.substance: Maintainability of the plan rather than of the code: nothing is lost, but the reshape is sized wrong at the start, and mis-sized work is where the pressure to cut tests comes from.
presentation.actionability: Direct: the affected files are named and the records are additive.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The design material is the focus file list, which exists to be exhaustive about what the worker opens. Naming fewer files than the work touches is a gap in it.

addressed_details.response: Six focus-file records added, one per affected component test file not already named: WORK:file-rd48342t9m (views.rs), WORK:file-t7cmkd9n1h (content_rendering.rs), WORK:file-v81jc6xs9c (theming.rs), WORK:file-30ge1mxghq (line_selection.rs), WORK:file-1h44rej5j7 (styling_hooks.rs) and WORK:file-ydp6wbya56 (reference_cases.rs). Each says what its file covers and why the reshape reaches it. A single directory-level record was weighed and set aside: work_file is file-granular by schema, and a per-file relevance line is what a directory entry could not carry.

content:
Pre-work session record: what the three reviewers developed, resolved against the sources, or set aside. No activity description was changed by activity development; each was examined and left as written, and the two edits this session made to activity text came out of finding resolution instead.

**Resolved against the sources**
- `Diff` as the live state's name reads as the crate's concrete domain noun rather than an abstract or metaphor label, so the Code Whisperer's rename-before-defining rule does not fire and activity WORK:activity-s1m3wbpec7's glossary entry is not a meaning imputed to a generic word. ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8's detail (`dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl`) shows the name was steered to at draft maturity beside `DiffAnalysis` and `DiffViewer`, which read as one family.
- The engine rename needs no requirement of its own: a rename changes no behavior, and the new options value is already required by REQT-7tk9vxv9wd (Building a live diff), which names every field it carries. Checked against the full area 4.0 text in `.project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:139-158`.
- The no-write-during-render discipline survives the move. `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:70-86` compares a basis on read rather than writing during rendering, and `rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/folding.rs:181-201` encodes the property as tests, so it is a contract under the Contract Verification Gate rather than a comment. Activity WORK:activity-9b867dj9sw names it and cites its line.
- The module named for the retiring trigger does not outlive it: activity WORK:activity-9b867dj9sw moves the expanded folds out of it and activity WORK:activity-gx60bkawf4 retires the trigger, leaving nothing behind in `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs`.
- Every `work_ref.file` value on this unit is a bare filename resolving to exactly one file, checked against the repository at capture time: `dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl`, `diff-viewer.reqts.jsonl`, `20260915.diff-viewer-component.workUnit.jsonl`, `rust-dioxus-port.workEpic.jsonl`. Correct under the pointer rubric's first verdict.
- The scope boundary states what is out: ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh carries the per-region close and the reset boolean as recorded exclusions, and activity WORK:activity-bx7yxakmx2 names the first of them.

**Prior art worth knowing**
- Two viewers over one live diff, which REQT-dxbaat20ja needs, already has its mounting shape: the theming work built a two-viewer test at commit `ee5ea56`. Carried here rather than as an open item, since it saves a search through an 815-line file and asks nothing of the worker.

**Set aside as unanchored**
- Whether the engine's function and output stay publicly exported once an app reaches them through the live diff. Nothing requires either way; it is the worker's call.
- How the fold basis reckons a reset once the trigger's counter is gone. Craft, entrusted.
- Whether the live diff's module will pass the size target `#prevent-megacode-files` sets. The worker carries that principle and splits as it writes.
- How a value reaches a test out of a mounted component. Raised as advice WORK:advice-qf0vfmktm4 and dismissed: a worker opening `rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/mounted_app.rs`, which the focus files already name, meets the limit on sight.
evidence: Each bullet above carries the citation for its own check, read at capture time. The activity descriptions were read from the committed .workUnit.jsonl; no narrower reading of any of the six was found that would satisfy its words and miss its intent, so none was developed.

body:
Pre-work is closed. Three reviewers seated, five findings raised and resolved, three sign-offs approved, and the in-scope requirement statuses moved to NEXT. The unit is work-ready and no code changed.

**Commits**
- `1f6872f` files the independent analysis from all three reviewers before any dialogue.
- `7008aa4` triages each finding to in-review with its presentation and venue.
- `3e7e673` gives the live diff, its options and the hook pair element records of their own.
- `3511bb9` scopes the four existing architecture records the work changes.
- `402b38e` names one position-and-line-number relation for the three answers that cross it.
- `2e99833` dismisses the test-harness advice and keeps its one durable line.
- `4323447` matches the focus files to the component test reach.
- The commit carrying this entry approves the sign-offs and moves the requirement statuses.

**Clarifications**
- Whether the live diff belongs under the viewer's component or wants one of its own: put as a key question, and the default under ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh was left standing.
- Whether the hand-off interaction survives the change: collapsed to a default against ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn's detail and `rust-dioxus/src/diff_viewer.rs:119-127`. One call remains, made by a different actor, so ARCH-atczcqvdsz keeps its identity and swaps its caller.
- Assent to build according to the in-scope requirements was given in dialogue and, per the pre-work protocol, is recorded nowhere else; no requirement's maturity moved because of it.

**Decisions**
- WORK:advice-qf0vfmktm4 was dismissed rather than carried, after the stakeholder asked whether a practical worker would not simply figure it out. Three factors settled it, and the first was an error of mine: WORK:file-3g4hd4ep2n already carried the harness fact in its relevance line, so the advice restated the plan back to itself. The lesson generalizes past this unit: before filing a recommendation, check whether a focus file's relevance line already says it.
- The four existing architecture records are scoped now but keep their current text; they change with the code in activity WORK:activity-s1m3wbpec7 rather than ahead of it. New element records went in ahead of the code, matching how the two decisions were recorded.
- Requirement status prep moved fourteen records to NEXT: area 4.0 with every child, and the two amended area 2.2 children whose IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION no longer matched their text.

**For the reviewer**
- The post-work sign-offs are seated and pending for the same three reviewers.
- Criterion WORK:crit-d5vagb7xpe is the one whose verification has to be deliberate: a dropped engine test case during the rename leaves the build green.
- The pass's own coverage trail is WORK:advice-f08kwnj9z8; what pre-work examined and set aside is there rather than in this report.

**For the next worker**
- A toon patch to a `.project` record needs the row's current `__rev`, and guessing one is rejected outright; the rejection reports the on-disk value, so an unprojected read of the row first is the cheaper path.
- `presentation.context` on a finding record is capped at 400 characters and the cap is easy to overshoot by a few; measure the text before the write rather than after the rejection.
- The repository has no project-level `.mcp.json`; toon reaches this project through global configuration.
- Seven of ten files under `rust-dioxus/tests/diff_viewer/` build a viewer through props this unit removes, and each now has its own focus-file record saying why.
